question: Identify an example of plasma as a state of matter.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Neon sign bulbs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Neon sign bulbs are an excellent example of plasma as a state of matter.
 
• Plasma is created in neon sign bulbs when an electric current passes through the gas, ionizing it and creating plasma.
 
• The plasma in neon sign bulbs emits light, which is characteristic of neon signs.
 
• Plasma is the fourth state of matter, distinct from solid, liquid, and gas, and is created under high-energy conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Plasma**

 
 
• Plasma is known as the fourth state of matter, consisting of a collection of free-moving ions and electrons.
 
• It is formed at very high temperatures when gases are ionized.
 
• Examples of plasma include the Sun, stars, lightning, and neon signs.
 
• Plasma is distinct from the other states of matter due to its unique properties such as electrical conductivity, magnetic fields, and the ability to emit light.
 
 
 
• **Neon**
 
 
• Neon is a noble gas that is colorless, odorless, and inert under standard conditions.
 
• It is used in neon signs where it emits a bright orange-red light when electrified.
 
• Neon signs work by passing an electric current through the neon gas, which ionizes the atoms and creates plasma.
 
 
 
• **Ionization**
 
 
• Ionization is the process by which an atom or molecule gains or loses electrons, forming ions.
 
• This process is fundamental in the formation of plasma.
 
• Ionization can occur through various means such as heating, electric fields, or radiation.
